text.p: Photran Corp said Thursday it will receive $4.5 million under a sale leaseback financing transaction with NBD Leasing using the company's P1000 coating line as collateral.
It is structured as a three-year full payout lease with a 50 percent balloon payment due at the end of the lease term.

Chief financial officer Paul Fink said, "Terms require that we collateralize the balloon payment with an offsetting amount of marketable securities. As a result, our net proceeds will be $2.3 million."

Fink said the transaction should provide "sufficient cash to enable the company to get its new P-1000 coating production line and facility online and to adequately support the market development and working capital requirements related to the new product introductions we have planned during the next 12 months."

Photran chief executive officer David Stevenson said "the market for the company's ITO (coating) products has improved during the past 45 days. We anticipate that the ITO market will continue to be strong at least through the third quarter of 1997."
Stevenson also said representatives from the company's largest customer, Wintek Corp, are now on site to witness the final assembly and test of the PVAC coating system it is supplying.

"We now anticipate that to accommodate the delays in the completion of Wintek's new Taiwan factory we will operate the PVAC machine under contract in our factory for several weeks prior to shipment," the executive added.
Photran develops and manufactures optical and electrically conductive thin film coated products.
